matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: When relocating a matchstick, keep its original orientation (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal) unchanged; you may only change its position, not rotate it. This prevents creating symbols that cannot be formed with the given stick direction.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you move a stick from one character to another, ensure the stick’s orientation stays the same.
matchstick.example: Treating a diagonal stick as a vertical one and using it to form an I, which yields an invalid character.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick must be relocated; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick without placing it elsewhere. This enforces the core rule of the puzzle.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of planning a move, verify that you are only moving a single existing stick.
matchstick.example: Adding an extra stick to a numeral to turn V into M, which violates the one‑stick‑move constraint.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After the move, every symbol (numeral or operator) must still be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a permitted operator (+, -, =). This guarantees the final equation is syntactically correct.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After deciding on a move, check that each affected character remains a recognized symbol.
matchstick.example: Leaving a V with a single diagonal, which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Convert the transformed Roman numerals to Arabic values and confirm that the two sides of the equation are equal. Visual validity alone is insufficient; the numeric equality must hold.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have a candidate transformed equation, compute its numeric values before finalising the answer.
matchstick.example: Accepting a visually valid equation like "X = IV" without checking that 10 ≠ 4.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: X and V must never be left with only one diagonal after a move; a single diagonal is not a valid Roman numeral. Any removal of a diagonal from these symbols must be compensated by adding another stick to keep them valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you consider removing a diagonal from an X or V, reject that move unless you simultaneously add a diagonal to preserve the character.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from an X and leaving a lone diagonal, which is invalid.

matchstick.title: Cross‑numeral stick transfer
matchstick.principle: A stick may be moved from one numeral to another, but both the source and destination must remain valid Roman numerals after the move. This ensures the transformation does not create illegal symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you think about taking a stick from one numeral to help another, verify that the donor numeral still forms a legal numeral.
matchstick.example: Taking the only vertical stick from an I and moving it to a V, which eliminates the I entirely.

matchstick.title: Within‑numeral stick repositioning
matchstick.principle: A stick can be relocated to a different position within the same numeral, changing its shape (e.g., turning V into X) while keeping the numeral valid. This is the key move for many puzzles where a single character’s value changes.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a single‑stick move can alter a numeral’s internal geometry without involving another character.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal within a V so that the two diagonals cross, thereby converting V (5) into X (10).

matchstick.title: Equality sign preservation
matchstick.principle: The equation must contain exactly one '=' sign after the move; you cannot turn '=' into another operator or remove it. This maintains the required structure of an equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before moving any stick that belongs to '=', ensure the sign will still have two horizontal sticks.
matchstick.example: Removing one horizontal from '=', turning it into a '-' and leaving the equation without an equality.

matchstick.title: Operator-to-numeral stick transfer
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from an operator to a numeral, the operator must remain a valid operator after the move (e.g., '-' must stay '-' or become '+'). This prevents the operator from disappearing or becoming an unrecognised symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If you consider taking a stick from '+' or '-', check that the resulting operator is still recognised.
matchstick.example: Taking the only horizontal stick from '-' and leaving no operator between two numerals.

matchstick.title: Source numeral must retain at least one stick
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick out of a numeral, the source numeral must still contain at least one stick; you cannot take the sole stick from an I or otherwise leave a numeral empty. This guarantees that every character remains a valid Roman numeral after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before moving a stick from any numeral, verify that the numeral will still have a valid shape after removal.
matchstick.example: Moving the single vertical stick from an I, causing the I to disappear and making the expression invalid.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model often checks only visual validity of symbols and forgets to compute the numeric values.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always convert the final Roman numerals to Arabic numbers and compare both sides before finalising the answer.

matchstick.why_it_happens: When a stick is removed from an operator like '-', the operator disappears, reducing the total number of operators.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never remove the only stick from a '-' or '+'; ensure the operator remains present after the move.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Moving a stick from an operator can leave it in a shape that no longer matches '+', '-', or '='.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After moving a stick from an operator, check that the remaining sticks still form a recognised operator.

matchstick.description: Removing the only stick from a numeral (making it empty)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes treats a numeral as a container of sticks and removes its sole stick, forgetting that the numeral would cease to exist.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Before moving a stick from a numeral, ensure the numeral will still have a valid representation (at least one stick) after removal.
